toolchain.backend: direct Metal command encoder; no WGPU device or session

workload.warmup: five discarded turns; timed session is recreated from the initial state, then remains resident for 40 timed turns
workload.timed_region: one command buffer and host wait per resident turn
workload.validation: finite state/covariance, positive covariance diagonal, covariance symmetry; reject-before-store

notes: The Mech kernel is the generic compiler artifact from hosts/gpu/fixtures/ekf-kernel.mec; no EKF-specific operation is used.
WGSL is used only as the backend-neutral interchange for Naga WGSL-to-MSL translation. No WGPU runtime or command path is created in MECH_METAL_ONLY mode.

The timed session is recreated after warmup, matching the Mojo control's fresh-state boundary. Source/artifact/scalarization, Metal pipeline creation, warmup, and final readback are outside the resident throughput timer.
The direct checked and unchecked outputs were compared with an independently executed scalar Mech reference after 40 turns; the maximum absolute error was 1.221e-4.

The default Mech scalar IR emits explicit fused multiply-add expressions. The opt-in MECH_AUDIT_DISABLE_FMA control measured 389.535 M/s checked and 390.424 M/s unchecked in one run; it is retained as an arithmetic-fairness audit, not as the default Mech lane.

The Mojo reference was built with --fp-mode contract=off. Its checked loop also enqueues a fault-buffer memset and maps the fault buffer after every turn, while this direct Metal session clears and reads a shared two-word status buffer directly. The 422.702 versus 244.493 checked result therefore is not an isolated language/kernel comparison until those compiler and status-path boundaries are matched.
The generic optimizer retains zero products so 0 * NaN and 0 * Inf remain observable to integrity predicates; this is covered by a unit test.

audit_controls.purpose: isolates arithmetic contraction from the checked/status transport path; not a replacement for the default lane
